Subject: RFP follow-up: recovery windows and evidence artifacts

Marcus,

Thanks for the submission earlier this week. The procurement and resiliency team reviewed Redwood's RFP packet and have two follow-up items we need clarified before our next evaluation:

1) For your warm-standby and active-passive options, can you provide a concise matrix mapping: recovery initiation trigger, expected RTO, expected RPO, user-visible degraded features, and the typical operator actions required?

2) We requested evidence of a multi-region failover rehearsal in the last 12 months. Can you point us to the artifact(s) and indicate whether the rehearsal included KV cache warm-up testing for production prompt distributions?

We need this by Monday EOD PST to stay on our vendor shortlist. If easier, a short call with an operations engineer would also work.

Regards,
Lydia Park
Director, Infrastructure Resilience
Sentinel Bank

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-25T12:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: recovery windows and evidence artifacts

Lydia — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I've attached a one-page matrix plus a diagram that should map directly to your ask. Attachment: service_continuity_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet) and playbook-diagram.png.

Quick mapping (summary):
- Trigger: regional outage detected by our health-check aggregator (automated) OR on-call operator-initiated based on customer impact.
- Warm-standby (recommended for most customers): typical RTO = 10–20 minutes for control plane + 1–3 minutes for sessions relying on KV cache when prefix warm-up enabled; RPO = near-zero for metadata + up to 60 seconds for in-flight token buffers depending on commit frequency. User-visible impact: minor increased tail latency and temporary rate-limited throughput during ramp. Operator actions: confirm traffic shard routing, optional manual cache pre-warm step (we automate when GRPC session patterns are known).
- Active-passive switchover (full region failover): typical RTO = 5–15 minutes for API availability if cold KV cache; 2–5 minutes if KV cache snapshot and prefix caching are available; RPO = 0–30 seconds depending on replication policy. User-visible impact: brief request errors during DNS/edge routing changes; potential transient inconsistencies for streaming completions. Operator actions: failover button in Console (automated rollback hooks), monitor replay queues, verify model variant compatibility.

On the rehearsal evidence: last yearly rehearsal was run on 2026-11-16 and included the following artifacts: playbook run log, metrics export, and a sample KV warm-up script used against a reduced traffic profile. The rehearsal purposely exercised the KV warm-up path for the top 12 customer prompt prefixes (by token volume) — results and notes are in the attached spreadsheet and the SharePoint link below.

If you want a short deep-dive with our ops engineer, I can schedule Marcus/Ben/Grace for a 30-minute slot tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Principal — Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): service_continuity_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet); playbook-diagram.png (image)

Subject: DR rehearsal notes for Sentinel follow-up (internal)

Team,

Short bullets to include in the RFP supplement:
- KV cache warm-up: we ran prefix pre-warm for the top 12 prefixes representing ~78% token volume; median warm-up time to steady-state was ~90s in rehearsal environment (see matrix column WarmupMedian).
- Replication: metadata and model state are replicated with multi-AZ sync; token buffer commits are throttled at 1s intervals during peak ingestion to bound RPO.
- Test scope: rehearsal exercised our smart routing fallback (regional -> secondary region), DNS TTL manipulations, and load-balancer draining to simulate active-passive cutovers.
- Evidence: runbook export, Grafana snapshots (latency/throughput), Playbook recording (screen capture), and the warm-up script. Link them in the attachments.

Recommended phrasing for the RFP: "Redwood's rehearsal was a full run-through of multi-region failover with KV cache warmup exercised against production prompt distributions scaled to 10% traffic — artifacts include runbook export, metric captures, and the warm-up automation script."

Ben
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
